title: Elevated end user self-check
intro: User and elevated-duty checks, plus one App C point.

questions.prompt: An elevated account you no longer need should be:
choices: Removed or reduced. Access stays justified.
Kept because it was hard to get.
Shared with the whole team for convenience.
Written on a sticky note under the keyboard.
questions.rationale: Least privilege and removal of access are §11 duties. Elevated use may also be audited.

questions.prompt: The access-control principle to remember first is:
choices: Least privilege.
Everyone gets admin on Fridays.
Longer passwords replace all other controls.
Classification labels are optional on RESTRICTED documents.
questions.rationale: G3 §11.1 starts from least privilege. Labels and handling still matter under §10.

questions.prompt: Clear desk and clear screen sit mainly in:
choices: S17/G3 §13 physical and environmental security.
Appendix D filing codes.
The canteen roster.
Section 3 normative references only.
questions.rationale: §13 covers secure areas and equipment habits, including clear desk and clear screen.

questions.prompt: Classified material you need to send should be:
choices: Marked and sent on the channel local rules allow, with encryption when the rule requires it.
Attached to a personal webmail account.
Posted in a team chat with no label.
Copied onto an unlabelled USB “just for the meeting”.
questions.rationale: §15.2 and §12 govern transfer and cryptography. Follow the local rule if it is stricter.

questions.prompt: A suspicious message was opened. Your first learning point is:
choices: Report through the departmental path. Do not wait for a private investigation to finish.
Delete it and hope.
Forward it to friends so they can test the link.
Post screenshots on social media.
questions.rationale: §18: report. A tabletop is for practice. A real event uses the live ISIRT path.

questions.prompt: You administer a task next to a Tier 2 system. Which App C theme applies?
choices: Independent checks of privileged accounts at least every six months, and MFA for interactive privileged logon where feasible.
No extra control, because App C is only for websites.
A public bug-bounty in your own name.
Skipping passwords because MFA exists somewhere else.
questions.rationale: Those are App C §11 controls for Tier 2, and Tier 3 inherits them. Confirm the tier with the owner.
